question: Which statement best describes generative AI?

options.A: It guarantees accurate answers when supplied with enough information.
options.B: It generates content from learned patterns but may produce inaccurate or unsupported information.
options.C: It functions only by retrieving exact passages from verified databases.
options.D: It independently determines whether every output is legally compliant.

question: You've used an AI tool to help complete a work assignment. How would you assess the reliability of its output before using it?

options.A: I would trust the output if it sounds professional.
options.B: I would review it for obvious mistakes.
options.C: I would identify claims that need verification, check appropriate sources, and acknowledge remaining uncertainty.

question: Your organization has approved an AI assistant. A colleague wants to use it to prepare a routine meeting summary, while another wants it to make final employee disciplinary decisions. What would you recommend?

options.A: Use AI for both tasks because the organization has approved the platform.
options.B: Avoid AI for both tasks because it may make mistakes.
options.C: Use AI to support the meeting summary with human review, but do not delegate final disciplinary authority to the assistant.

question: An employee wants an AI assistant to create a professional summary of a project meeting for department leadership. Which instruction would be most effective?

options.A: Summarize this meeting.
options.B: Write a professional summary using these approved notes.
options.C: Using these approved meeting notes, create a 200-word leadership summary covering decisions, action items, owners, and deadlines. Flag any missing information rather than inventing it.

question: An AI assistant produces a report that is too technical for the intended audience. What is the best next step?

options.A: Accept it because the assistant has completed the request.
options.B: Ask it to simplify the language.
options.C: Specify the intended audience, desired reading level, report structure, and information that must remain accurate, then review the revision.

question: Which principle best describes effective context management when interacting with an AI system?

options.A: Provide all available organizational information regardless of relevance.
options.B: Include relevant, authorized information necessary for the task while minimizing unnecessary or sensitive data.
options.C: Avoid providing any context because AI systems should infer the details.
options.D: Include personal information whenever it may improve the response.

question: Which type of task is generally the strongest candidate for initial AI-assisted workflow improvement?

options.A: A high-stakes decision requiring professional judgment and no human review.
options.B: A repetitive, well-defined task with clear quality criteria, appropriate data safeguards, and human oversight.
options.C: A task involving confidential records uploaded to an unapproved platform.
options.D: A process with no measurable outcomes or defined requirements.

question: Your department prepares a weekly operational report using approved internal data. You want to integrate AI into the reporting process. What is the best approach?

options.A: Automate the entire report and distribute it without review.
options.B: Use AI to draft portions of the report and manually check a few figures.
options.C: Identify appropriate reporting steps, use an approved AI tool, validate the figures against source data, review the narrative, and document human approval before distribution.

question: A team introduces an AI assistant to help prepare customer service responses. Employees report that drafting is faster, but managers are concerned about quality. How should effectiveness be evaluated?

options.A: Measure only the number of responses generated.
options.B: Compare the time required before and after implementation.
options.C: Compare drafting time, accuracy, corrections, customer outcomes, and staff review requirements against a defined baseline.

question: An AI assistant produces a summary of new industry regulations, including several compliance requirements. How should the employee validate the information?

options.A: Assume the information is accurate because the system lists sources.
options.B: Compare the summary with another AI assistant.
options.C: Check the claims against current authoritative regulatory sources, confirm applicability and effective dates, and correct unsupported statements.

question: An AI-generated project summary references a policy deadline that does not appear in the source document. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Keep the deadline because the AI appears confident.
options.B: Remove the deadline without checking whether it exists elsewhere.
options.C: Investigate the claim using the original document and authoritative references, then correct or remove it based on verified evidence.

question: Which criteria provide the strongest basis for evaluating the quality of an AI-generated workplace deliverable?

options.A: Response speed, length, and visual appearance.
options.B: Confidence of wording and professional tone.
options.C: Accuracy, completeness, relevance, consistency with requirements, and appropriate evidence.
options.D: Number of paragraphs and amount of technical vocabulary.

question: An employee needs to summarize records containing customer information. The organization has an approved enterprise AI platform, but data handling restrictions apply. What should the employee do?

options.A: Upload the records to their personal AI account.
options.B: Remove customer names and assume the records are safe to upload.
options.C: Confirm that the intended data and use are permitted in the approved platform, apply required safeguards, and seek authorization when necessary.

question: A recruitment team uses an AI tool to help summarize candidate qualifications. A manager notices that candidates with similar qualifications are being described differently in ways that may reflect bias. What should the team do?

options.A: Continue using the summaries because the AI system is automated.
options.B: Ask the system to produce more neutral descriptions.
options.C: Investigate the differences using job-relevant criteria, review affected outputs, document potential bias, and involve appropriate personnel before continuing to rely on the process.

question: Which statement best describes responsible use of AI under organizational policies?

options.A: Employees may use any AI system if their work improves.
options.B: Publicly available AI tools are automatically approved for workplace use.
options.C: Employees should use authorized tools, follow applicable security and data policies, and report suspected violations through established procedures.
options.D: Compliance is the responsibility of the technology department alone.

question: When is human review particularly important in an AI-supported process?

options.A: Only when an AI system produces a visibly incorrect answer.
options.B: When decisions have significant consequences for safety, rights, employment, finances, or other high-impact outcomes.
options.C: Only when the AI tool is unfamiliar to employees.
options.D: Never, provided the system has been tested.

question: An employee discovers that an AI-generated financial report contains a calculation error that could affect an upcoming management decision. What should happen next?

options.A: Ignore the error if the overall report appears reasonable.
options.B: Correct the calculation without informing anyone.
options.C: Prevent the uncorrected information from being used, verify the affected calculations, notify the responsible personnel, and follow the organization's escalation procedures.

question: A department introduces an AI assistant to recommend which customer complaints should receive priority attention. Managers retain final decision-making authority. What is the most appropriate accountability arrangement?

options.A: Allow the AI assistant to make final decisions because it generates the recommendations.
options.B: Ask managers to review recommendations, without establishing consistent review criteria.
options.C: Establish documented decision authority, review criteria, escalation requirements, and records of human decisions and overrides.

question: An employee is preparing a presentation for organizational leadership. The work includes summarizing research, creating an outline, verifying statistics, and approving final recommendations. Which division of work is most appropriate?

options.A: Delegate all tasks, including final approval, to AI.
options.B: Use AI to produce an outline and complete everything else manually.
options.C: Use AI to assist with authorized summarization, outlining, and drafting while retaining responsibility for verification, interpretation, recommendations, and approval.

question: Which practice best supports effective coordination between employees and AI systems?

options.A: Treat AI-generated output as completed work that requires no further review.
options.B: Clearly define task responsibilities, expected outputs, verification steps, and human decision authority.
options.C: Allow employees to determine responsibilities after the AI system produces its results.
options.D: Minimize human participation whenever AI can generate an answer.

question: An AI assistant prepares a draft training guide for employees. The guide will be distributed across several departments. What should occur before publication?

options.A: Publish the guide because the content is organized and professional.
options.B: Review its grammar and formatting.
options.C: Validate accuracy, learning objectives, instructions, accessibility, organizational relevance, and applicable policies before approval.

question: Your organization introduces an approved AI tool that you have not used before. Which response best describes your approach to developing the necessary skills?

options.A: I would avoid learning the tool unless required.
options.B: I would attend the required training and practice the demonstrated functions.
options.C: I would identify relevant learning needs, complete appropriate training, practice with permitted tasks, seek feedback, and monitor whether my performance improves.

question: Your team changes its established workflow to incorporate an approved AI assistant. Some processes are unfamiliar, and you initially experience difficulty. What would be your approach?

options.A: Continue using the old process without exploring the new workflow.
options.B: Follow the required training and ask for assistance when needed.
options.C: Identify the difficulties, practice the approved workflow, seek feedback, and communicate problems or improvement opportunities to the appropriate team members.

question: An AI-supported reporting workflow has been operating for three months. Employees report that it saves time, but several steps still require unnecessary corrections. What is the strongest improvement strategy?

options.A: Continue using the workflow unchanged because it saves time.
options.B: Ask employees to suggest improvements.
options.C: Review performance data and employee feedback, identify recurring errors, test targeted improvements, and monitor their effects on quality and efficiency.
